I can't give you a dose for vitamin D. Amounts for any supplement are one for a doctor or dietitian, and they can check your actual levels first, which matters more than a gym-goer's average.

For context, vitamin D supports bone health and muscle function, and many people run low in winter or when they're indoors a lot. A blood test is the clean way to know whether you need anything. Bring it up at your next checkup, and I'll keep the training side moving. What are we working on this week?
